events.title: Founding of Saint Petersburg
events.description: Tsar Peter the Great founded Saint Petersburg on the Neva River, building the Peter and Paul Fortress on Hare Island during the Great Northern War.
events.significance: The city became the capital of the Russian Empire for two centuries and symbolized Peter's drive to modernize Russia and open it to Europe.

events.title: Birth of the Brooklyn Bridge Opening Week Context
Golden Gate Bridge Opens to Pedestrians
events.description: The Golden Gate Bridge in San Francisco opened to pedestrian traffic on this day, with vehicle traffic beginning the following day.
events.significance: At the time it was the longest suspension bridge main span in the world and became an enduring symbol of San Francisco and American engineering.

events.title: Operation Anthropoid: Attack on Reinhard Heydrich
events.description: Czechoslovak resistance fighters Jozef Gabčík and Jan Kubiš, trained in Britain, attacked SS official Reinhard Heydrich in Prague. He died of his wounds on June 4.
events.significance: Heydrich was a chief architect of the Holocaust. Nazi reprisals included the destruction of the villages of Lidice and Ležáky.

events.title: Death of Jawaharlal Nehru
events.description: Jawaharlal Nehru, the first Prime Minister of independent India, died in New Delhi after serving since 1947.
events.significance: His death ended the leadership of a key figure of the Indian independence movement and the Non-Aligned Movement, ushering in a transition to Lal Bahadur Shastri.
